name: 1Password
tagline: Password manager for logins, passkeys, secrets, and secure sharing

pricing.notes: Official personal pricing page checked; public page lists annual effective pricing, while 2026 price-change notices may affect renewals and regions.

tiers.name: Individual
tiers.limits: 1 person; unlimited passwords and devices; 1 GB document storage
tiers.notes: $2.99/month is the advertised first-year annual price for new annual customers; regular renewal pricing applies afterward.

tiers.name: Families
tiers.limits: Up to 5 family members; unlimited passwords and devices; 1 GB document storage/user
tiers.notes: $4.49/month is the advertised first-year annual price; additional family members may cost extra.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; advertised annual rate is a first-year promotion
pricing.hiddenCosts: The discounted annual amount is introductory and auto-renews at the then-current regular price; taxes may be added and family seats beyond the included 5 can increase the bill

verdictSummary: A basic encrypted vault is buildable, but browser autofill, mobile apps, passkeys, sharing, recovery, audits, and trust make this a dangerous thing to replace casually.
coreLoopDIY: Create a local encrypted vault, generate passwords, search entries, and optionally sync the encrypted database with a cloud drive.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because password managers are one place where reliability and audited security beat saving a few dollars.

priorArt.name: KeePassXC
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source local password manager and the safest DIY-adjacent alternative.

alternatives.name: Bitwarden Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited passwords, passkeys, secure notes, and one-person sharing; built-in TOTP and full reports cost extra.

alternatives.name: Vaultwarden
alternatives.desc: Passwords, passkeys, notes, sharing, and reports on your server; polished recovery support becomes your problem.

rejectedAlternatives.name: KeePassXC
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Excellent local secrets and passkeys; secure multi-user sharing is deliberately absent.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Padloc
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The live site hides a stalled repo: last commit March 2025 and production self-hosting docs never really arrived.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Proton Pass Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Passkeys and unlimited logins are free; secure vault sharing and broader monitoring are paid.

notes: A crucial honesty page: buildable in theory, but replacing a password manager is high-risk.
prompt:
Build me a local encrypted password vault to replace 1Password, CLI-first. Requirements:

- A single-binary CLI in Go using filippo.io/age for encryption and Argon2id
  (golang.org/x/crypto) to derive the key from my master passphrase. Use the
  library primitives exactly as documented, invent no crypto.
- The vault is one encrypted file at ~/.vault/vault.age holding JSON entries:
  name, username, password, URL, notes, updated timestamp.
- Commands: add, get <name> (copies to clipboard, clears it after 20 seconds),
  ls, gen (32-char random password), edit, rm.
- Fuzzy name matching on get; never print a password to stdout unless --show
  is passed.
- vault backup writes a date-suffixed copy of the encrypted file to a folder
  set in .env; it is already encrypted, so any cloud drive can sync it.
- Import from a 1Password CSV export so I can migrate in one command.
- Everything local: no server, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: browser autofill, passkeys, and secure sharing. Those are why
  people pay 1Password; if I need them the honest move is KeePassXC or
  Bitwarden, say exactly that in the README.
- README: a five-line threat model, how key derivation works, and a warning
  that losing the master passphrase loses everything, there is no recovery.
